title: Spanish colonization of the Americas
summary: After Christopher Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492, Spain founded Santo Domingo in 1498, home to the first cathedral, hospital and university in the Americas. Columbus's repartimiento system gave settlers land and native labour. Hernán Cortés entered Tenochtitlán in 1519, and the smallpox the Spanish brought took a heavy toll. Spain lost its last American colonies in 1898, giving up Cuba and Puerto Rico after the Spanish–American War.

uncertainty.note: Begins with Columbus's first landfall in 1492 and ends with the 1898 Spanish-American War, though most mainland colonies achieved independence between 1810 and 1826.

where.modern_name: Colonial City of Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic (seat of first Spanish colonial government in the Americas)
where.historical_name: Santo Domingo, Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, Spanish Empire

importance.justification: Began Spain's long rule over much of the Americas, with devastating effects on Indigenous peoples.

audience_note: Covers colonial conquest, forced labor (encomienda), severe demographic collapse of indigenous populations from violence and introduced epidemics, and transatlantic enslavement.
